messages:
alex: FYI AcmeCorp (private VPC) asked if we can let them manage per-org + per-key rate policies inside their VPC. They want burst controls and the ability to host the policy blob themselves. Any blockers?

samir: They want policy stored in their S3 and signed by their KMS key. Two big questions: where to enforce (control plane vs local agent) and how we prevent them from shooting themselves in the foot.

maria: Safety is the main risk. If a customer uploads a policy that accidentally sets huge limits, it could starve shared infra. My thought: allow only caps (no routing overrides), and enforce platform-level upper bounds.

jess: Enforcement options: 1) control-plane validates and pushes resolved rules to the data-plane; 2) local-agent inside VPC reads signed blob and enforces locally. Local-agent reduces attack surface to our control plane but we need a secure signing flow.

alex: Proposal sketch: local-agent model. Customer uploads signed JSON policy to their S3. local-agent (running in customer's VPC) pulls, verifies signature against a stored customer public key (we record key fingerprint during onboarding), converts rules into token-bucket params, and enforces. Control plane still receives telemetry + a read-only copy for audits.

jen: UX question: how do we communicate to enterprise support and devs that policy is "customer managed"? Console should show an orange badge and a preview of "effective limits" (platform default vs customer override). Also allow an ops "shadow mode" where we only report violations for N days before enforcement. :eyes: 

samir: Example policy format (first pass):

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "scope": "org",
  "rules": [
    {"subject": "org:acme", "limit_rps": 100, "burst": 200},
    {"subject": "api_key:abcd1234", "limit_rps": 10, "burst": 20}
  ],
  "nonce": "2026-03-15T12:00:00Z",
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG"
}
```

maria: Enforcement semantics we should standardize: token-bucket per-key with a parent org bucket. If the org bucket is depleted, all child keys are constrained. Policy should include action: reject (429), queue (up to X ms), or soft-limit (log + 200 with Warning header). Default to reject.

alex: Need a safety valve: local-agent must respect a platform-supplied hard cap for each host/cluster that cannot be overridden by customer policy. That prevents local policies from bypassing host protection during overload.

ratebot: policy blob fetched from s3://acmecorp/redwood-rate-policy.json, signature verified (key-id: kms://projects/acme/keys/ratepolicy), pushed to agent acme-agent-01, applied 2 rules.

jess: Telemetry contract: emit metrics: redwood.policy.source, redwood.policy.applied_ts, redwood.enforce.rejected_total, redwood.enforce.queued_total, redwood.policy.signature_ok (bool), last_signature_check, effective_limits{org,api_key}. Dashboards should allow quick drilldown by api_key and by host.

samir: Precedence rules need to be explicit: platform_override > customer_policy > default_platform_policy. Console should compute and display the effective limit and the rule that caused it.

alex: Open action items: (1) maria: prototype local-agent signature verification + parent/org bucket logic; (2) jess: mock console diff + shadow-mode UX; (3) samir: draft policy schema, precedence, and fail-open/fail-closed modes. I'll write a short design doc.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rate-limiter-agent v0.9 -> canary -> acme-vpc-1

maria: Started prototyping. Will drop notes and a small sequence diagram in #eng-platform shortly.

jen: Also: we need to document onboarding steps for customers: key registration, S3 path, TTL for polices, and emergency rollbacks.

alex: Good. Keep the thread focused on security + enforcement semantics; for billing/quotas we can follow-up. Thanks.
